ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p533/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p533/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p533/r1.claim: Moses fled Egypt fearfully and prayed for protection from the oppressive people.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.speaker: الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.claim: Hasan, Ata, and Ikrima hold that all of al-Qasas is Meccan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.anchor: وروي عن الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة أنها مكية كلها

TABATABAI:28:15/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:15/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:15/r1.claim: This section recounts events after Moses reached maturity that led him to leave Egypt for Midian.
TABATABAI:28:15/r1.anchor: فيه ذكر بعض ما وقع بعد بلوغه أشده فأدى إلى خروجه من مصر وقصده مدين

RAZI-FULL:v24p203/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p203/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p203/r4.claim: Moses left fearing for his life from Pharaoh’s people, watching to see whether they would pursue and seize him.
RAZI-FULL:v24p203/r4.anchor: أي خائفا على نفسه من آل فرعون ينتظر هل يلحقه طلب فيؤخذ

RAZI-FULL:v24p203/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p203/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p203/r5.claim: Knowing there was no refuge except God, Moses sought refuge with Him and asked to be saved from the oppressors.
RAZI-FULL:v24p203/r5.anchor: ثم التجأ إلى الله تعالى لعلمه بأنه لا ملجأ سواه

RAZI-FULL:v24p203/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v24p203/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v24p203/r6.claim: Rāzī says this shows Moses’ killing of the Copt was not a sin: otherwise Moses would be the oppressor, not the people seeking to kill him in retribution.
RAZI-FULL:v24p203/r6.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن قتله لذلك القبطي لم يكن ذنبا

BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r7.claim: Moses left immediately, with no provisions, mount, or companion.
BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r7.anchor: {فخرج منها} (س بيرون رفت درهمان دم ازان شهر بي زاد وراله ورفيق)

BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r8.claim: He left in a state of fear for his own safety.

BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r9.claim: He watched for pursuers to catch up or attack on the road.
BURSEVI:v6p285#2/r9.anchor: {يترقب} لحوق الطالبين والتعرض له في الطريق

BURSEVI:v6p285#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p285#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p285#3/r1.claim: Moses asks God to free him from Pharaoh and his people and protect him from their catching up with him.

BURSEVI:v6p285#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p285#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p285#3/r2.claim: God answered Moses' prayer and saved him, as the account will explain later.
BURSEVI:v6p285#3/r2.anchor: فاستجاب الله دعاءه ونجاه كما سيأتي

BURSEVI:v6p285#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p285#3/r3.speaker: بعض العارفين
BURSEVI:v6p285#3/r3.claim: God may place a servant in a terrible ordeal to make him flee from everything to God; the ordeal becomes a means to the intended arrival.
BURSEVI:v6p285#3/r3.anchor: قال بعض العارفين : إن الله تعالى إذا أراد بعبده أن يكون له فردا

BURSEVI:v6p285#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p285#3/r4.speaker: بعض العارفين
BURSEVI:v6p285#3/r4.claim: The one who flees to God in fear of a trial finds the Beauty of the All-Merciful and recognizes events as means of arrival.
BURSEVI:v6p285#3/r4.anchor: فلما فر إليه خائفا من الامتحان وجد جمال الرحمن وعلم أن جميع ما جرى

BURSEVI:v6p285#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p285#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p285#3/r5.claim: The Masnavi story illustrates this: fear of a night watchman drives a lovesick youth into a garden, where he finds the beloved he had long sought.
BURSEVI:v6p285#3/r5.anchor: جست از بيم عسس وشب بباغ يارخودرا يافت

BURSEVI:v6p285#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p285#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p285#3/r6.claim: What appears an enemy can be medicine and a guide to the Beloved; escape from it should lead one to seek God's kindness.

BURSEVI:v6p285#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p285#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p285#3/r7.claim: A cited Masnavi analogy says a snake's venom sustains the snake but kills a human, showing that adversity's effect depends on the recipient.

STUDYQURAN:28:21/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:21/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:21/r1.claim: Moses is again fearful and vigilant, as after striking the Egyptian, because he expects Pharaoh’s forces may catch and kill him.
STUDYQURAN:28:21/r1.anchor: Fearful and vigilant (cf. v. 18) is the same way Moses is described after he struck and killed the Egyptian

STUDYQURAN:28:21/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:21/r2.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:28:21/r2.claim: Moses’ prayer highlights his reliance on God and his recognition that God alone is his refuge.
STUDYQURAN:28:21/r2.anchor: Moses’ prayer is understood to highlight his reliance upon God and his realization that God was his only refuge

TABATABAI:28:18-21/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:18-21/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:18-21/r7.claim: Moses’ flight in fear supports the view that he did not consider the accidental killing of the Copt a crime for which he was culpable.
TABATABAI:28:18-21/r7.anchor: فيه تأييد أنه ما كان يرى قتله القبطي خطأ جرما لنفسه

THALABI:v7p242/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p242/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p242/r14.claim: Moses left Pharaoh's city afraid and watching for pursuit, and prayed for deliverance from the unjust people.
THALABI:v7p242/r14.anchor: فخرج موسى منها أي من مدينة فرعون خائفا يترقب ينتظر الطلب قال رب نجني من القوم الظالمين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p366#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p366#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p366#2/r1.claim: They identify the wrongdoing people as the polytheists, the people of Egypt.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p366#2/r1.anchor: {قال رب نجني من القوم الظالمين} قال ابن عباس ومقاتل: يعني المشركين، أهل مصر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r1.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Moses left without knowing which direction to take, and God prepared the way to Midian for him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p367/r1.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: ذكر أنه خرج على وجهه {خائفا يترقب} ما يدري أي وجه يسلك، فهيأ الله له الطريق إلى مدين

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:20-21/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:20-21/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:20-21/r4.claim: Moses left afraid and expecting pursuit.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:20-21/r4.anchor: فخرج منها خائفا يترقب } ينتظر الطلب

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:20-21/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:20-21/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:20-21/r5.claim: The oppressive people from whom Moses seeks rescue are Pharaoh’s people.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:20-21/r5.anchor: قال رب نجني من القوم الظالمين } قوم فرعون

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584#2/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p584#2/r6.claim: Moses went out of the city.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r1.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r1.claim: Qatāda says Moses feared being killed for the killing and watched for pursuers.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r1.anchor: {خائفا يترقب} [القصص: 18] قال قتادة: خائفا من قتله النفس، يترقب الطلب.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r2.claim: Moses asks God to rescue him from the unjust people.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p585/r2.anchor: {قال رب نجني من القوم الظالمين} [القصص: 21] قوله عز وجل:

QASHANI:28:20-22/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:20-22/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:20-22/r4.claim: His departure means undertaking struggle in God and maintaining presence and watchfulness; he fears their dominance and seeks refuge in God from their oppression.
QASHANI:28:20-22/r4.anchor: { فخرج } بالأخذ في المجاهدة في الله ودوام الحضور والمراقبة { خائفا } من غلبتهم، متلجئا إلى الله في طلب النجاة من ظلمهم

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:20/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:20/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:20/r1.claim: Once the Egyptian’s killer became known, Pharaoh ordered measures to capture Moses; a well-wisher ran to warn him and advise escape, so Moses left the city for Midian.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:20/r1.anchor: Hz. Mûsâ’nın iyiliğini düşünen bir kişi koşarak gelip bu durumdan onu haberdar etti ve şehirden çıkıp gitmesi için nasihatte bulundu

QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r4.claim: Moses left Egypt fearing they would track him and watching lest pursuit catch him.
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r4.anchor: خرج من مصر { خائفا } أن يقتفوا أثره

QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r5.speaker: قيل
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r5.claim: Another explanation is that Moses watched for God's sufficiency and aid.
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r5.anchor: وقيل { يترقب } الكفاية والنصرة من الله

QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r6.claim: Moses prayed to be rescued from the unjust people.
QUSHAYRI:v2p432/r6.anchor: ودعا الله فقال : { نجنى من القوم الظالمين }

BURHAN:v1p41/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p41/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p41/r4.claim: The account of Moses after the Night Journey connects Muhammad’s visible signs and reports of past events as proofs of prophethood; alternatively, his escape from Egypt parallels Moses leaving in fear.
BURHAN:v1p41/r4.anchor: أو أنه أسرى بمحمد إلى ربه كما أسرى بموسى من مصر حين خرج منها خائفا يترقب

BURHAN:v3p27/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.claim: Repeated tellings of Moses and Pharaoh differ in wording, order, and detail because each version carries a nuance found only there; unlike earlier scripture's separate single tellings, Joseph's story is collected in one sura.
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.anchor: فقد يوجد في ألفاظها زيادة ونقصان وتقديم وتأخير

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p330/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p330/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p330/r1.claim: He was watchful and afraid, expecting harm to befall him.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p330/r1.anchor: {خائفا يترقب} أي ينتظر سوءا يناله منهم.

SAMIN-DURR:28:21/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:21/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:21/r1.claim: Yataraqqabu means that Mūsā awaited guidance and God’s succor.
SAMIN-DURR:28:21/r1.anchor: أي: يترقب هدايته وغوث الله إياه

ZAJJAJ:v4p137#2/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p137#2/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p137#2/r7.claim: Moses feared being caught and killed, and watched for signs or tracks.
ZAJJAJ:v4p137#2/r7.anchor: أي يرقمب أن يلحقه في يقتله

ZAJJAJ:v4p138/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p138/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p138/r1.claim: The oppressive people are Pharaoh's people.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p110/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p110/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p110/r3.claim: The reform exception fits the Queen of Sheba, who left sun-worship and submitted to God; Moses was already a believer, and his confession of wrong concerned killing the Egyptian, not a change from disbelief.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p110/r3.anchor: فإنها ظلمت نفسها بكفرها وسجودِها للشمس من دون الله، ثم بدّلت حُسْناً بعد سوء، فأسلمتْ لله رب العالمين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p92/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p92/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p92/r5.claim: Fear frames al-Qaṣaṣ from Musa's mother's alarm to Musa's fear after killing the Egyptian and his fearful flight from the city, while Naml mentions fear only at the staff miracle.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p92/r5.anchor: في سورة القصص، كان جو القصة مطبوعاً بطابع الخوف الذي يسيطر على موسى، عليه السلام

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r1.claim: Fear continues in al-Qaṣaṣ as Musa prays for rescue, receives reassurance in Midian, fears Pharaoh's killing and denial, and asks Aaron to assist him; this contrasts with Naml's brief, less fearful story.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r1.anchor: وهذا الطابع - أعني طابع الخوف - يبقى ملازماً للقصة إلى أواخرها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p71/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p71/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p71/r2.claim: Fear frames al-Qasas from Moses' mother's fear through Moses' flight and prayer for rescue, until a man in Midian reassures him; al-Naml presents a more honorific setting.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p71/r2.anchor: بل إن جو الخوف كان مقترنا بولادة موسى عليه السلام، فقد خافت أمه فرعون عليه

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p89#5/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p89#5/r1.speaker: author
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p89#5/r1.claim: Moses fled fearing the killing and watching for pursuers who might seize him.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p89#5/r1.anchor: ﴿ فخرج منها خائفا يترقب ﴾ من قتل النفس يترقب أن يأخذه الطلب

ALUSI-FULL:v20p59/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59/r1.claim: Moses left the city in compliance with the warning.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59/r1.anchor: فخرج منها ( أي من المدينة ممتثلا

ALUSI-FULL:v20p59/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p59/r2.claim: He was afraid and watchful for pursuers to catch up with him.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r1.claim: Moses left the city fearing and expecting pursuit; the oppressive people he asks God to save him from are the unbelievers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r1.anchor: خائفا يترقب} أي: ينتظر الطلب، {قال رب نجني من القوم الظالمين} الكافرين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r2.claim: In the story, Pharaoh sent people after Moses and told them to ride the mountain passes, since Moses did not know the route.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p199/r2.anchor: وفي القصة: أن فرعون بعث في طلبه حين أخبر بهربه فقال اركبوا ثنيات الطريق

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:21-23/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:21-23/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:21-23/r1.claim: Moses left the city afraid and watching for someone pursuing him; he prayed to be rescued and protected from the wrongdoers catching up.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:21-23/r1.anchor: لحوق طالب. { قال رب نجني من القوم الظلمين }

BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r11.claim: Moses promptly leaves the city after recognizing the man’s warning as credible from its surrounding signs.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r11.anchor: مبادرا { منها } أي المدية لما علم من صدق قوله مما حفه من القرائن

BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r12.claim: He fears Pharaoh’s people and repeatedly turns to see whether anyone is following him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p474/r12.anchor: في الجهات ينظر هلى يتبعه أحد

BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r1.claim: Moses addresses God as the benefactor who created and nurtured him and bestowed many kinds of kindness.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r1.anchor: ايها المحسن إلي بالإيجاد والتربية وغير ذلك من وجوه البر

BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r2.claim: Najjinī means rescue me; the word derives from najwa, a high place inaccessible to everyone.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r2.anchor: أي خلصني , مشتق من النجوة , وهو المكان العالي الذي لا يصل إليه كل أحد

BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r3.claim: The wrongdoers invert proper order by killing the undeserving despite their own power.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r3.anchor: الذين يضعون الأمور في غير مواضعاها فيقتلون من لا يستحق القتل مع قوتهم

BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r4.claim: God answers by directing Moses toward Midian along the main road; his pursuers miss him because they assume a fugitive would use side routes or cross-country paths.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p475/r4.anchor: فاستجاب الله له فوفقه لسلوك الطريق الأعظم نحو مدين , فكان ذلك سبب نجاته

DURR-FULL:v6p401/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p401/r8.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v6p401/r8.claim: Al-Suddi recounts that a Copt exposed Moses to Pharaoh; while searchers pursued him through the byways, the warning man came, then an angel on horseback led Moses toward Midian after he prostrated in fear.
DURR-FULL:v6p401/r8.anchor: عن السدي قال: ذهب القبطي فافشى عليه: أن موسى هو الذي قتل الرجل فطلبه فرعون وقال: خذوه

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Moses headed toward Midian, having never met a man there before and knowing no route; he trusted his Lord.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : فخرج منها متوجها نحو مدين لم يلق رجلا قبل ذلك ، وليس له بالطريق علم الا حسن ظنه بربه

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960/r2.claim: Al-Suddī says an angel on horseback, carrying a spear, met Moses in the side paths, forbade him to prostrate, and guided him toward Midian.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960/r2.anchor: عن السدي فخرج منها خائفا يترقب قال رب نجني من القوم الظالمين فلما اخذ في بنيات الطريق جاءه ملك على فرس بيده ، عنزة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960/r3.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says Moses did not know which way to go; God guided him to Midian, and he left without provisions, servants, or a mount.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2960/r3.anchor: عن محمد بن اسحاق قال : فذكر لي انه خرج على وجهه خائفا يترقب ، ما يدري اي وجه يسلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r7.claim: Taraqqub literally means waiting, derives from observing something’s condition, and is metaphorically used here for caution.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r8.claim: Moses’ prayer is a بدل اشتمال of his keeping watch, since watchfulness includes praying to God for rescue.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r8.anchor: لأن ترقبه يشتمل على الدعاء إلى الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r9.claim: The unjust people are Pharaoh’s people: they were polytheists and sought to kill Moses in retaliation for an accidental killing, which reason and law do not warrant.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r10.claim: The episode teaches that God chooses whom He wills, prepares means to fulfill His purpose, and rescues His chosen messenger; upright conduct and love of truth disclose that care to the perceptive observer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r10.anchor: وأن الناظر البصير في آثار ذلك التدبير يقتبس منها دلالة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r11.claim: The signs in Moses’ story invite the Meccans to consider Muhammad’s character and their dealings with him, as the verse asks whether they reason about his lifetime among them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r11.anchor: وفي ذلك كله مثل للمشركين لو نظروا في حال محمد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r12.claim: The warning hints that Muhammad too will leave Mecca and that God will save him from his oppressors.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p96/r12.anchor: إيماء إلى أن رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم سيخرج من مكة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r3.claim: Moses escaped unseen, took the main route to Midian, and traveled alone on an unfamiliar road, trusting God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r3.anchor: وخرج بحكم فزعه ومبادرته إلى الطريق المؤدية إلى مدين وهي مدينة قوم شعيب عليه السلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r4.speaker: السدي ومقاتل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r4.claim: Al-Suddī and Muqātil say God sent Gabriel or another angel to guide Moses to Midian and gave him a staff, perhaps his own.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r4.anchor: قال السدي ومقاتل: فروي أن الله تعالى بعث إليه جبريل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r5.claim: Another report says he took the staff for shepherding in Midian; the author calls this sounder and more frequent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r5.anchor: وروي أن عصاه إنما أخذها لرعي الغنم في مدين وهو أصح وأكثر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r6.speaker: ابن جبير والناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r6.claim: Ibn Jubayr and others say Midian was eight days from Egypt.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r6.anchor: وبين مدين ومصر مسيرة ثمانية أيام قاله ابن جبير والناس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p282/r7.claim: Midian was ruled by someone other than Pharaoh.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211/r1.claim: Moses left Egypt in fear; the commentary says it already explained this in the sura.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211/r1.anchor: أي من مصر خائفا وقد مضى تفسيره القصص

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p211/r2.claim: The oppressive people are the polytheists of Egypt.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p226#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p226#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p226#2/r1.claim: On learning of Pharaoh's plot, Moses left Egypt alone, unused to a life of flight after comfort, luxury, and status; he looked around fearfully.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p226#2/r1.anchor: خرج من مصر وحده، ولم يألف ذلك قلبه، بل كان في رفاهية ونعمة ورئاسة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p226#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p226#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p226#2/r2.claim: Moses asks God to save him from Pharaoh and his elite, whom Ibn Kathir identifies as the unjust people.

JISHUMI:v8p5484/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5484/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5484/r3.claim: Taraqqub means waiting and keeping watch; raqīb derives from the same root.

MUQATIL:28:20-23/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:20-23/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:20-23/r3.claim: Moses feared being killed and watched for the pursuers as he fled.
MUQATIL:28:20-23/r3.anchor: يعني ينتظر الطلب، وهو هارب منهم

MUQATIL:28:20-23/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:20-23/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:20-23/r4.claim: The oppressors are Egypt’s polytheists; God answered by sending Gabriel to direct Moses toward Midian and giving him the staff.
MUQATIL:28:20-23/r4.anchor: يعني المشركين، أهل مصر، فاستجاب الله عز وجل له

NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#3/r1.claim: Moses left the city in fear, watching for an attack on the road or someone pursuing him to kill him.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#3/r1.anchor: التعرض له في الطريق أو أن يلحقه من يقتله

NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p231#3/r2.claim: The unjust people Moses asks to escape are Pharaoh's people.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r6.claim: يترقب means watching for or expecting pursuit.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r7.claim: Moses asks God to rescue him from the unjust people.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:20-22/r7.anchor: قال رب نجني من القوم الظالمين
